Single cell organisms aren't as dumb it makes us comfortable to believe. There are some fairly interesting studies on memory involving microorganism. Too lazy to go dig source atm but the experiment goes:

Use puff of air at specific interval on microrganism. Organism begins to "anticipate" response and braces itself (adaptive behavior). Remove stimulus and observe the organism continues to anticipate it or remembers the experience.

So, essentially, to boil it down, memory in anything (a cell, an animal, a bacteria, anything living I suppose) is possible even without a brain. Unless the nucleus is like a brain? Idk, do cells have brains?

It seems so. That's why I love things like slime molds because they challenge the idea of what we view as thinking individuals. They are just a clump of cells but sometimes they decide to behave like an individual and coordinate a transformation into a bud to release spores. But then...they'll go back to acting like a random blob of biomass if not dispersing completely into its unassuming individuals. How do they decide to do this? How do they coordinate who will make spores, who will control movement, who will get food? How do they sense gravity or know the reproductive bud needs to grow upwards. They can communicate all these things to each other but we don't know how.
It's simply beautiful. I imagine what it might be like to live as a mold spore, and jokes aside, it seems like it would be a very social endeavor.

Siphonophores are pretty cool as well. They can form these fantastically complex structures but they are still just groups of cells living colonially with no apparent central authority to direct them. How does a colony of cells become "I" instead of "we". I am remain philosophically and scientifically intrigued by the bounds of individuality.

Divide that by 3600 to get degrees and you get about 8 degrees of arc, so theoretically they might be able to "see" that there are two people standing side by side instead of one, provided they're standing within a couple of meters away.
